Shell commands matching keyword `*'

(( ... )) - Evaluate an arithmetic expression.
. - Run the commands of a file in the current shell.
: - Do nothing, successfully.
[ - Evaluate a conditional expression.
[[ ... ]] - Evaluate a conditional expression, without word splitting.
alias - Define or print aliases.
break - Leave a for, while, until or select loop.
case - Run the commands of the first pattern that matches.
cd - Change the working directory.
command - Run a command, passing over shell functions, or describe it.
continue - Start the next pass of a for, while, until or select loop.
declare - Set variables and their attributes.
disown - Remove jobs from the shell's job table.
echo - Write the arguments to standard output.
eval - Run the arguments as a command line.
exec - Run a command in place of the shell, or redirect the shell.
exit - Leave the shell.
export - Put variables in the environment of the commands it runs.
false - Do nothing, unsuccessfully.
fg - Bring a job to the foreground.
for - Run commands once for each word of a list.
for (( - Loop under the control of arithmetic expressions.
function - Define a shell function.
getopts - Parse options from the arguments.
help - Show how to use the shell's own commands.
history - Print or change the command history.
if - Run commands when a condition holds.
jobs - List the shell's jobs.
kill - Send a signal to processes or jobs.
let - Evaluate arithmetic expressions.
local - Define variables local to a function.
mapfile - Read lines into an indexed array.
printf - Print arguments under the control of a format.
pwd - Print the working directory.
read - Read one line and split it into fields.
readarray - Read lines into an indexed array; the same as `mapfile'.
readonly - Make variables read-only.
return - Leave a function or a sourced file.
select - Choose words from a numbered menu.
set - Set shell options and positional parameters.
shift - Shift the positional parameters.
shopt - Set and unset shell options.
source - Run the commands of a file in the current shell.
test - Evaluate a conditional expression.
time - Report how long a pipeline takes.
trap - Run commands when the shell meets signals or events.
true - Do nothing, successfully.
type - Tell how the shell would run a name.
typeset - Set variables and their attributes; the same as `declare'.
umask - Print or set the file mode creation mask.
unalias - Remove aliases.
unset - Remove variables and functions.
until - Run commands for as long as a condition fails.
wait - Wait for jobs and return their status.
while - Run commands for as long as a condition holds.
{ ... } - Run a list of commands as a group.

cd: cd [-L|[-P [-e]] [-@]] [dir]
    Change the working directory.
    
    Makes DIR the working directory, or $HOME when no DIR is given. `cd -' goes
    back to $OLDPWD.
    
    Options:
      -L	keep symbolic links in the new path (the default)
      -P	resolve symbolic links in the new path
      -e	with -P, fail when the new path cannot be resolved
      -@	accepted, with no effect
    
    Exit Status:
    0 when the directory changed, otherwise non-zero.
set: set [-abefhkmnptuvxBCEHPT] [-o option-name] [--] [-] [arg ...]
NAME
    wait - Wait for jobs and return their status.

SYNOPSIS
    wait [-fn] [-p var] [id ...]

DESCRIPTION
    Wait for jobs and return their status.
    
    Waits for each ID, a process ID or a job spec, and returns its status. With
    no ID, waits for every job the shell started and returns 0. Only a job this
    shell started can be waited for.
    
    Options:
      -f	wait until each ID ends, not only until it changes state
      -n	wait for the next job to end and return its status
      -p var	store in VAR the ID whose status is returned
    
    Exit Status:
    The status of the last ID, or failure when an ID or an option is invalid.

SEE ALSO
    bash(1)

IMPLEMENTATION

echo - Write the arguments to standard output.
eval - Run the arguments as a command line.
exec - Run a command in place of the shell, or redirect the shell.
exit - Leave the shell.
export - Put variables in the environment of the commands it runs.
